VERVISTA SKYLINE IN KOCHI REPORTS STRONG BOOKINGS AS RATES CLIMB

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

Kochi: Vervista Skyline, the residential project by Praara Realty, has drawn strong buyer interest, with 74 percent of its apartments already booked. The project has 1,914 apartments in total and is registered under RERA number P76409377495.

Prices have moved up notably since the first sales: the selling rate per square foot has risen from ₹9,450 at launch to Rs. 13,100 at present, so the launch rate is the earlier and lower one.

The developer has also updated the unit profile. The average apartment size was first reported as 1,195 square feet, but that figure has been revised to 1,010 square feet, and the revised size replaces the original in all project material.

The campus will include 4 swimming pools alongside landscaped open areas and other resident facilities. Construction is advancing to schedule, and possession is planned in 2024.

"We are pleased with the response from homebuyers, and our focus remains on delivering quality and keeping to the handover timeline," said a senior official of Praara Realty.

Interested buyers can contact the project sales office in Kochi for details.

Total patient revenue for 2023-24 was first reported as Rs 20.0333 billion. That figure has since been revised, and the revised ₹2,12,733 lakh replaces the original as the official number. Inpatient services contributed 67 percent of total patient revenue. The hospital also reported total operating expenses of INR 2129.6 crore for running costs, and a net surplus of ₹3,243 million after all costs.

Outpatient demand remained heavy, with 236,250 visits and consultations. The daily inpatient load is shown in the table.

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|

The trust's sister facility, Partner Sampath Hospital, also reported its figures. Partner Sampath Hospital has 530 beds and recorded 53,650 inpatient admissions in 2023-24. Its inpatient services earned INR 1527.8 crore in the same year.

**Vasdhi Ltd: snacks and beverages maker keeps margins healthy while it expands**

Vasdhi Ltd, a packaged snacks and beverages company headquartered in Bhubaneswar, was founded in 2000 and today runs ten offices and plants across its footprint. Our desk summarises the reported numbers below.

| Metric | fiscal 2024 | fiscal 2025 |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue | Rs. 45,110 lakh | ₹5,143 million |
| Operating profit | ₹767 million | INR 51.4 crore |

**Reading the table.** Revenue grew from fiscal 2024 to fiscal 2025, though operating profit moved in the opposite direction, which suggests input and distribution costs rose faster than sales in the later year. We would not call this alarming for a business still building out its network, but it deserves monitoring.

**The following year.** In the year right after fiscal 2025, revenue rose 25%, a strong pace for a mid-sized FMCG name. Operating expenses in that same year came to 89% of revenue, leaving a thin operating cushion. Separately, total expenses including finance costs, depreciation and tax were INR 680.5 cr, which is a broader measure and should not be confused with the operating-expense ratio just quoted.

**Outlook.** Management has guided to revenue of Rs. 7,415 million in fiscal 2027, a forecast and not a result. The company also plans capital expenditure of Rs 45.2 cr for a new facility, which should add capacity to support that target. We see execution on cost control as the key swing factor.

Founded in 1963, it now has a presence in 6 cities. Revenue slipped in the latest year, yet margins held up and the company stayed solidly profitable. Ruhtek Kisan FPO Posts Better Soybean Yield Despite Modest Rains

RAICHUR - Ruhtek Kisan FPO, a farmer cooperative in Raichur district, has closed its rabi 2023 season with a slightly improved soybean yield, according to the field report compiled by an agri-extension NGO worker.

Members cultivated soybean over 4,415 acres. The average yield was 7.9 quintals per acre, up from 7.6 quintals per acre last season. Rainfall during the season was 210 mm. The cooperative, registered in 2011, keeps a warehouse with a capacity of 11,300 tonnes.

On prices, the government MSP stood at ₹4,892 per quintal, the average mandi modal price at harvest was Rs 5,040, which is the open-market rate and a different thing from the cooperative's own sales, and the FPO realised an average of ₹5,290 per quintal on its soybean sales, all in one season in which collective selling clearly paid off.

Total cultivation cost for all members together, covering seed, fertiliser, labour and irrigation, came to ₹12.5386 crore.

The neighbouring Surtek Kisan Samiti fared less well. Surtek Kisan Samiti reported an average yield of 7.5 quintals per acre and an average cultivation cost of ₹12,350 per acre. Its realised price was Rs. 4,230 per quintal, well below what Ruhtek Kisan FPO obtained.

Field workers say better bargaining through the FPO explains much of the difference.
